page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-16GB is a virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor, featuring two shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with 50 GB of SSD capacity. The CPU configuration consists of two physical cores with one thread per core, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core execution capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both ranking in the top tier. However, multi-threaded scaling and overall system throughput show notable limitations. The multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU score, and PassMark memory score fall into the bottom tier. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also constrained, reflecting the shared CPU allocation model. Memory bandwidth remains moderate, averaging 67.19 GB/sec for large-block read operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance multi-core processing. It is well-suited for lightweight web serving, development environments, small-scale caching, and basic LLM inference tasks using small models. It is less appropriate for heavy database operations or highly parallelized computing tasks due to its shared CPU allocation and lower multi-threaded benchmark scores.
